clue.text: Ditched aircraft, drifting on tides

parts.note: a jet is a type of aircraft

indicators.note: letters that drift wander out of their places, so on and tides are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plane has come down in the sea and floats about on the tide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drifting' suits the ditched plane bobbing on the sea, but it is the anagram signal for the two words after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To jettison is to throw overboard or discard, so jettisoned things have been ditched.

clue.text: Exercise for press going after parish feature

indicators.note: the word for press comes after the parish feature in the answer

parts.note: the village pump was a traditional feature of an English parish
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Someone presses a case for something in the parish, perhaps at a council meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The village pump, the old shared water supply, was a standard sight in an English parish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumping iron is the idiom for lifting weights, a form of physical exercise.

clue.text: Garments from the centre of Belarus for Poles

indicators.note: the centre of a seven-letter word is its fourth letter, picked from Belarus

parts.note: pro means for, as in pros and cons
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Clothing has been exported from central Belarus to Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like the nationality but gives the compass points N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Aprons are garments tied over the front to protect clothes.

clue.text: Tool for data collection

definitions.meaning: a hand tool with a rough surface for smoothing or shaping
a named collection of data stored on a computer or in a folder

explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the abrasive hand tool and a set of stored records.

clue.text: Gathering herbs, medic may get dirty

indicators.note: gathering pulls things into a heap, so the letters of herbs and medic are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A doctor out picking herbs ends up with muddy hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathering' seems to be what the medic does but signals the anagram of HERBS MEDIC; 'may get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Besmirched means soiled or sullied, literally or in reputation, so it serves as an adjective for dirty.

clue.text: Sacrifice made by uncle in beach buggy?

indicators.note: the uncle's name goes inside the rearranged beach
buggy, as in faulty or crazy, tells us to rearrange the letters of beach

parts.note: Uncle Tom, from the novel Uncle Tom's Cabin, gives the name Tom

explanation.surface: An uncle has built something on a sand buggy at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buggy' looks like a beach buggy, the sand car, but it means faulty and signals the anagram; 'in' places the uncle's name within it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was an ancient Greek sacrifice of many cattle, now any large-scale slaughter.

clue.text: As a bear is turned — turned inside out

indicators.note: the reversed is goes inside what is left of turned
with its outside letters out, only the middle of the second turned remains

parts.note: turned means the little word is is read backwards

indicators.note: this word means the letters it governs are turned round, so they are read backwards

explanation.surface: A bear rolled over and was flipped inside out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' appears twice: first as a reversal signal, then as fodder whose outer letters are dropped by 'out'; 'inside' sets the reversed word in what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursine is the adjective meaning like or relating to bears.

clue.text: Date in Rome that is timeless

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: id est is the Latin for that is, abbreviated i.e.

explanation.surface: An appointment in Rome that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: T is the standard abbreviation for time, so 'timeless' removes it from ID EST.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides was a fixed day of the Roman calendar, the 15th or 13th of the month.

clue.text: Balance regarded as fit by French banker

parts.note: to fit out is to equip
a banker here is a river, something with banks; the Oise is a river in France

explanation.surface: A French bank official thinks the balance looks healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' in crosswords often means a river, since it has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipoise is a state of equal balance between forces.

clue.text: Being held back by breeder reactors was wrong

indicators.note: back means the letters found are read in reverse
being held by the phrase means the letters are found within breeder reactors

explanation.surface: Some nuclear process was being withheld by breeder reactors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being held' finds DERRE inside breeDER REactors and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake, so erred means was wrong.

clue.text: Work in hotel off A1

indicators.note: the abbreviation for work goes inside the rearranged hotel
off, meaning not right or gone bad, tells us to rearrange hotel

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A job at a hotel just off the A1, the main road north from London.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest road, which makes 'A1' look like a place, but it is the definition, meaning first-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-hole is dated British slang for excellent, just as A1 means first-rate.

clue.text: Stingy people with wealth that is invested

indicators.note: invested means placed within, so the abbreviation goes inside the word for wealth

parts.note: means are money or wealth, as in a man of means
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Misers with fortunes have put their money to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested' looks financial, but it signals a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Meanies are mean, ungenerous people, a synonym for stingy people.

clue.text: Trees with small globes

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
orbs are globes or spheres

explanation.surface: Some trees have tiny round fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorbs are trees of the rowan and service-tree family.

clue.text: Training some smart little monkeys

indicators.note: training shapes and rearranges, so the letters of some smart are reordered

explanation.surface: A trainer is teaching a few clever small monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' signals the anagram of SOME SMART.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmosets are small South American monkeys.

clue.text: What Coleridge's wedding guest did with suspect bones

parts.note: in The Rime of the Ancient Mariner the wedding guest is stopped by an old sailor, so he met a tar, a tar being a sailor
sus is British slang for suspect or suspicious

explanation.surface: A literary question about what happened to the wedding guest in Coleridge's poem and some dubious bones.
explanation.walkthrough: In Coleridge's poem a wedding guest is waylaid by the Ancient Mariner; tar is old slang for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The metatarsus is the group of five long bones in the foot.

clue.text: Sweet hubby does home work for powerful woman

indicators.note: to work something is to shape it, so the letters of the four words are reworked

explanation.surface: A dear husband does the housework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' looks like housework but signals the anagram of SWEET HUBBY DOES HOME. The phrase is from Rider Haggard's novel She, and is used humorously of a domineering wife.
explanation.definitionFit: She Who Must Be Obeyed is the title of Haggard's all-powerful queen Ayesha, applied jokingly to a commanding wife.

clue.text: Fairly deserving people? They're exceptional

parts.note: alludes to Dryden's line that only the courageous deserve the fair; those people are the only exception to a none, so they are exceptional

explanation.surface: A question about who deserves good things, answered with praise.
explanation.walkthrough: Dryden's Alexander's Feast says that only the brave deserve the fair; 'Fairly deserving' points to that line, and 'exceptional' is the exception made by 'but'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase from Dryden names the only people who deserve the fair, the exceptions to 'none'.

clue.text: See 15
For example, Flashman broadcast on the air

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of on the air are scattered

explanation.surface: Someone like Flashman is being broadcast on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Flashman is the cowardly, caddish hero of George MacDonald Fraser's novels. 'broadcast' fits 'on the air' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashman is a classic example of a protagonist lacking heroic virtues.

clue.text: A poet in action thawed out

indicators.note: the poet's name goes inside the word for action

parts.note: a deed is an action
Robert Frost was an American poet

explanation.surface: A poet takes action to warm things up.
explanation.walkthrough: FROST in DEED; the poet's name suits a clue about thawing.
explanation.definitionFit: Defrosted means having had the ice removed, thawed.

clue.text: Disk that's not a hit with artless party

parts.note: a flop is a failure, the opposite of a hit

indicators.note: art-less means the letters of art are removed from party

explanation.surface: A computer disk that failed to catch on at a plain, unsophisticated party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'artless' looks like an adjective for party but means PARTY without ART, leaving PY.
explanation.definitionFit: A floppy is short for floppy disk, the old flexible magnetic storage disk.

clue.text: Cast found in play area

definitions.meaning: to throw or hurl, as in casting or flinging something
the field on which a game is played, such as football

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to throw and the playing field for a sport like cricket or football.

clue.text: Tape transported by road for an infernal device?

indicators.note: transported means moved about, so the letters of tape are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tape is sent by road for some diabolical machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' rearranges TAPE into PETA, followed by RD.
explanation.definitionFit: A petard was a small bomb used to blow open gates, a hellish device, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Support one entrant, one of the first in a field

definitions.text: one of the first in a field

indicators.note: one entering, here the word for one entering the support

parts.note: a pier is a support, such as a pillar holding up a bridge

explanation.surface: Backing one competitor, who is among the first in the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrant' looks like a competitor but signals ONE going into PIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is among the first to explore or develop an area of work.

clue.text: Is there some wine left?

definitions.meaning: the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone asks if any wine remains in the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both the fortified wine from Oporto and the nautical term for left.

clue.text: Hollywood star with German pal

parts.note: mit is the German word for with
a chum is a pal

explanation.surface: A film star turns up with a German friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Mitchum was a Hollywood actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Mitchum was a leading Hollywood film star of the 1940s-60s.

clue.text: Milton's first poem displays style

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of Milton's is taken

parts.note: an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Milton's debut poem shows his manner of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a manner or style of doing something.

clue.text: Europe has nothing to lose changing currency

indicators.note: changing means the letters of Europe are rearranged once the letter for nothing has gone

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Europe has nothing to lose by switching money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose' tells us O is removed from EUROPE; 'changing' rearranges the remaining EURPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of India and several other countries.

clue.text: Ready for battle before introduction of slow bowling technique

indicators.note: the bowling technique comes before the next letter in the answer

parts.note: underarm bowling, with the hand below shoulder height, is a style of delivery in cricket

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter, here taken from slow

explanation.surface: A cricket team readies itself before a slow bowler comes on.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, bowling is overarm; underarm is a slow, old-fashioned style. 'Ready for battle' looks like a cricket description but defines the whole answer, read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Under arms means armed and ready to fight, as troops are.
